raw_case_text: A 26 year-old woman with no medical history of personal or family tuberculosis was admitted for a left sub-mandibular swelling which had appeared 12 months earlier. It began small then gradually increased in volume without alteration of the general condition. Many broad-spectrum antibiotics were attempted without any improvement. Examination showed a 5 cm painless, elastic left parotid mass, adherent to the skin and deeper layers, with mild inflammation of the overlying skin but without fistula or facial paralysis (Figure 1). Moreover, we found ipsilateral sub-mandibular lymphadenopathies. The contralateral parotid region was unremarkable. Otoscopy was normal and oral cavity examination showed neither left tonsillar deviation nor purulent secretions from the left Stensen's duct. The MRI showed a 4.6 cm, irregular and heterogeneous tumoral process of the deep lobe of the left parotid gland with a T1 hyposignal and a T2 hypersignal, and heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium injection (Figure 2). Fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of the mass was inconclusive. We, therefore, decided an exploratory extrafacial parotidectomy. In preoperative, parotid tissue appeared necrotic and purulent by places (Figure 3). Frozen section showed tuberculous lesions in both parotid and sub-mandibular lymph nodes. We, therefore, restricted surgery to a left lower pole parotidectomy. A check-up looking for second location tuberculosis (clinical examination, chest X ray, sputum analysis) was negative. The tuberculin skin test was positive at 12 mm. A prolonged (9 months) four drug antituberculous regimen (H: isoniazid, E: ethambutol, R: rifampicin and Z: pyrazinamid) was then started according to our usual protocol: 2 RHZE/7 RH. The evolution was satisfactory with no relapse after six years.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old female presented with a left submandibular swelling that had been present and enlarging for 12 months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 26-year-old female noticed a small swelling in the left submandibular area 12 months prior to admission that gradually increased in volume without constitutional symptoms. Multiple empirical courses of broad-spectrum antibiotics failed to reduce the mass.
subjective.past_medical_history: No personal or family history of tuberculosis. Multiple courses of broad-spectrum antibiotics without improvement.
subjective.review_of_systems: Denied weight loss, fever, or alteration of general health. Other systems, home medications, and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: 5 cm painless, elastic left parotid mass adherent to skin and deeper planes with mild inflammation of overlying skin; no fistula or facial nerve palsy. Ipsilateral submandibular lymphadenopathy present. Contralateral parotid normal. Otoscopy normal; oral cavity showed no tonsillar deviation or purulent discharge from Stensen duct.
objective.routine_investigations: Chest X-ray and sputum analysis showed no active pulmonary focus. Tuberculin skin test positive with 12 mm induration.
objective.advanced_workup: MRI: 4.6 cm irregular, heterogeneous tumoral process involving deep lobe of left parotid gland (T1 hypointense, T2 hyperintense, with heterogeneous gadolinium enhancement). Fine needle aspiration cytology was inconclusive. Exploratory extrafacial parotidectomy revealed necrotic and purulent parotid tissue intraoperatively; frozen section demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous lesions in parotid gland and submandibular lymph nodes. Restricted to left lower pole parotidectomy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Primary parotid tuberculosis with ipsilateral submandibular tuberculous lymphadenitis, confirmed by frozen section and histopathology demonstrating characteristic caseating granulomatous tuberculous lesions in parotid and nodal tissue in conjunction with a positive tuberculin skin test (12 mm induration). Workup for secondary pulmonary or systemic focus was negative. Management & Outcome: Underwent left lower pole parotidectomy followed by a 9-month 4-drug antituberculous regimen (2 months of isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol followed by 7 months of rifampicin and isoniazid: 2RHZE/7RH). Achieved complete clinical cure with no recurrence at 6-year follow-up.
